---
title: "Readings — Long-read library preparation"
---

The papers here are the ones that define the protocols in the deck. Read the methods sections:
the length of the molecule you get is decided there, and the exercises ask you to reason about it.

## PacBio

**Wenger AM, et al. (2019).** *Accurate circular consensus long-read sequencing improves variant
detection and assembly of a human genome.* Nature Biotechnology 37:1155–1162.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-019-0217-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0217-9) — **start here**

> HiFi reads. Look at how insert size and accuracy trade off, and which library choices the
> authors varied to find the balance.

**Travers KJ, et al. (2010).** *A flexible and efficient template format for circular consensus
sequencing and SNP detection.* Nucleic Acids Research 38:e159.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkq543](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkq543)

> The SMRTbell. Short and exact about the topology: find where the nuclease treatment is used
> and what it removes.

**Sharon D, et al. (2013).** *A single-molecule long-read survey of the human transcriptome.*
Nature Biotechnology 31:1009–1014.
[doi:10.1038/nbt.2705](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.2705)

> The first long-read isoform survey in human samples, and the origin of Iso-Seq. Read the cDNA
> preparation and note how full-length reads are defined.

**Al'Khafaji AM, et al. (2024).** *High-throughput RNA isoform sequencing using programmed cDNA
concatenation.* Nature Biotechnology 42:582–586.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-023-01815-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01815-7)

> The array idea behind Kinnex: why it was needed, and what it does to the throughput of
> isoform sequencing.

## Nanopore

**Jain M, et al. (2018).** *Nanopore sequencing and assembly of a human genome with ultra-long
reads.* Nature Biotechnology 36:338–345.
[doi:10.1038/nbt.4060](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4060) — **start here**

> How a human genome was sequenced with reads of hundreds of kilobases. The extraction and
> library methods are the point: find the steps that the authors changed to avoid shearing.

**Workman RE, et al. (2019).** *Nanopore native RNA sequencing of a human poly(A)
transcriptome.* Nature Methods 16:1297–1305.
[doi:10.1038/s41592-019-0617-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0617-2)

> Direct RNA on human samples. Look at the adapter chemistry and at what the authors say about
> input requirements and yield.

## Enrichment

**Gilpatrick T, et al. (2020).** *Targeted nanopore sequencing with Cas9-guided adapter
ligation.* Nature Biotechnology 38:433–438.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-020-0407-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0407-5)

> Cas9 enrichment from native DNA. Find the dephosphorylation step and check the reasoning in
> exercise E10 against the authors' own.

**Payne A, et al. (2021).** *Readfish enables targeted nanopore sequencing of gigabase-sized
genomes.* Nature Biotechnology 39:442–450.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-020-00746-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-00746-x)

> Adaptive sampling in practice on a large genome. Compare what the authors gain in enrichment
> with what they spend in pore time.
